newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOS SEEN STUCK UNLESS BEIGE BOOK SHOCKS.
newsitem.headline: OLOS SEEN STUCK UNLESS BEIGE BOOK SHOCKS.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) were seen in tight ranges ahead of more news on the U.S. economy, dealers said, after the prospect of new supply brought little life to the market on Monday.

The Belgian Treasury on Tuesday is due to offer OLO lines 13 (7.00 pct April 1999), 25 (5.00 pct March 2001), 24 (7.00 pct May 2006) and 16 (7.50 pct July 2008) in exchange for OLO lines 17 (6.25 pct November 1996) and 22 (7.50 pct January 1997).
"OLOs 25, 24 and 16 are a little bit sold because of the auction, but not much," one trader said. The yield on the benchmark OLO 24 was 6.57 percent in late trade on Monday.
The yield premium over Bunds was steady at 25 basis points. Late on Friday the yield was 6.78 percent. "The curve is a touch steeper, but nothing too spectacular," one trader said.

"This morning (OLOs) were a bit offered but this afternoon people have been buying everything," he added, noting the market expected U.S. and German bonds to remain steady until the publication at 1400 GMT on Wednesday of the publication of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book of economic activity.
Dealers said Belgium's 1997 budget should take centre stage at the end of September but for now the market remained driven by outside factors.
The budget in neighbouring France could provide more short term direction if it looked like the government was fudging its way to the Maastricht single currency criteria, one said.
"French traders seem rather calm about it all. But you have to remember that unlike Belgium a lot of French debt is held by London traders and they see things differently," he said.
"If France comes under pressure then we could suffer a bit too," he added.
